text:
anna: Quick flag - after landing int4 build for `gemma-lite-6b` I see the model spuriously emitting a function-call token sequence when summarizing multi-turn chat transcripts. FP16 baseline is fine.

ben: can you show minimal repro + diff? sounds like a tokenization / special-token collision.

anna: repro below. baseline = `gemma-lite-6b-fp16`, candidate = `gemma-lite-6b-int4-v2`. Note this is with `stream=false` and `function_call=auto` in the harness.

anna: ```bash
python eval/run_chat_eval.py --model gemma-lite-6b-int4-v2 --input tests/multi_turn_chat.jsonl \
  --max-tokens 128 --batch 1 --function-calling auto --stream false > out_int4.jsonl
python eval/run_chat_eval.py --model gemma-lite-6b-fp16 --input tests/multi_turn_chat.jsonl \
  --max-tokens 128 --batch 1 --function-calling auto --stream false > out_fp16.jsonl
```

anna: observed mismatch: on prompt id `chat-042` fp16 returns text summary, int4 returns "function_call": {"name":"save_conversation","args":"..."} with very high probability at token 47.

roxanne: interesting. is the `function_call` token a single special token in the tokenizer or a sequence?

anna: tokenizer shows `'<|fn_call|>'` is a single Vocab token id 50230. token ids for first 60 tokens match between builds, but at step 47 int4's top token is 50230 with p=0.93 while fp16 top token is 1194 (".").

ben: that smells like a projection/head-mix issue where a small subset of heads dominates softmax due to packing mis-accumulation. did you dump per-head logits?

anna: ran `--dump-logits-per-head` and attached head slices for tokens 44..50. head 9 and head 13 in int4 show extremely large positive bias on vocab index 50230. in fp16 those heads are neutral.

ci-bot: CI run `gemma-lite-int4-eval` queued, job id 7842.

roxanne: head-specific bias suggests either (1) quantization scale mismatch per-head, (2) permutation/order change in Q/K/V projection packing, or (3) stray accumulator reuse. which quant backend did converter use?

anna: converter v2.4 used per-head scale packing + stochastic rounding. commit = 3f8a2cdef. logs show `packed_head_order=interleave` for int4 path.

ben: try forcing `packed_head_order=contiguous` in runtime as quick test. if that changes behavior we know it's ordering.

anna: quick test done: with `packed_head_order=contiguous` the summary matches fp16. gap closes.

roxanne: ok that implicates ordering. maybe the attention kernel assumes contiguous head layout for the per-head scale table but converter emitted interleaved layout, so scales misaligned by head index. the effect would show up as a sharp vocab bias on certain heads.

anna: agreed. reproducer attached to GH issue #4599 with logits, per-head md5s, converter commit, and the diff outputs. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4599

ben: action items: 1) add runtime assert that `packed_head_order` matches converter metadata at load time 2) add unit test that simulates interleaved vs contiguous scale tables 3) hotfix converter to emit explicit metadata header for head layout and bump schema version 3->4.

roxanne: i'll own unit tests and the runtime assert. anna will make hotfix PR for converter. ben can review.

ops-bot: scheduled canary job `gemma-lite-int4-canary` on dev cluster at 01:15 UTC and pinned to converter commit 3f8a2cdef for validation.

anna: thank you all — will update GH issue with hotfix PR and attach canary results. :rocket:

ben: nice catch. also add a lint rule in converter to fail if it produces `interleave` without emitting layout header.

roxanne: noted. adding to checklist.

anna: closing thread for now, will reopen if new regressions appear.
